A One way ticket to the Red Planet

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Have you got what it takes to get a one way ticket to Mars

Summary:
Have you got what it takes to get a one way ticket to the Red planet Has science become a reality show? Five South Africans Divashen Govender, Kobus Vermeulen, Adriana Marais, Edwin le Grange and Alexandra Doyle have been shortlisted as part of a group of 100 participants from across the globe looking for a one-way ticket to Mars. In 2013, 2 000 people from across the globe initially applied to go to the red planet, a voyage scheduled to take place in 2018. Now the group has been fine-tuned to 100 There are 50 men and 50 women who successfully passed the second round. The candidates come from all around the world, namely 39 from the Americas, 31 from Europe, 16 from Asia, 7 from Africa, and 7 from Oceania. Is this crazy suicide mission or what or a bona fida science research project; a revival of the golden age of discovery where explorers left their homes to begin new civilisations ..the video used to inspire the 2000 people who initially signed is a mix between Survivors and The Hunger Games.

Further information:
The objective of Dutch non-profit Mars One is simple: to establish a permanent human settlement on the red planet. They will begin training candidates for space travel up until its 2024 planned launch, when – if all goes well – teams of successful candidates from around the world will form part of the first human colony on Mars. And a lot of people don’t think this is an impossibility – life on Mars -like South African, Elon Musk, founder of space transport services company SpaceX, who has said recently that he was hopeful that humans could be taken to Mars in the next 10 to 12 years. “I think it’s certainly possible for that to occur. The thing that matters long term is to have a self-sustaining city on Mars to make life multiplanetary. That will define a fundamental bifurcation of the future of human civilisation. We’ll either be a multiplanet species and out there among the stars, or a single-planet species until some eventual extinction event, natural or man-made.” Candidate,Adriana Marais, a PhD student in quantum biology at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, “What the first colonisers will do on Mars is really the pinnacle of four billion years of evolution, I would volunteer to leave my life on Earth behind to see what’s out there. I’m prepared to sacrifice my personal joys, sorrows and day-to-day life for this idea, this adventure, this achievement that would not be mine but that of all humanity.”  Candidate, Kobus Vermeulen, a 31-year-old from Pretoria has climbed Kili­man­jaro and skydived, said that Mars was the next big adventure. He has not romanticised the harsh realities of “yummy dehydrated army food” until the colony has established its food-growing mechanisms or that, if chosen, he would be leaving his old life behind. “In the end, you are exchanging all those things for new experiences on a new planet … you become part of humankind’s quest for long-term survival in what is, as it turns out, a very hostile universe.” Many of the South African candidates say that they would like to be buried on Mars, or to dedicate their bodies or organs to remaining crew members. But this may contaminate the planet and could also pose a problem to space science. With aid of visuals, artistic renditions of Mars, and real footage taken from the various missions we will explore how real this process will be and possible enlighten some of our candidates who despite ( apparently) rigorous research were not aware of the harshness of the Martian environment. Asked what they believed their days on Mars would involve, some said they would go for long walks to explore the planet, ­others that they would be growing food in Mars’s mineral-rich soil. Science and what has been discovered about Mars will be tested against some of the perceptions put out by Mars One. Out of the 100 chosen it will be 24 who eventually join the first settlement team, the ultimate Big Brother Challenge

Press Release:


Mars One
It’s the trip of a lifetime… a one way ticket to Mars, and three South Africans have been shortlisted to join the colony. Mars One is one of the space missions aiming to establish a permanent human settlement on the Red Planet. Several unmanned missions will be completed, establishing a habitable settlement before carefully selected and trained crews finally depart for Mars. Carte Blanche explores this extraordinary mission.


Script:


Divashen: its mind blowing to consider and then you look at the scale of the universe just outside our solar system and then you go outs ide our galaxy and then you get something that’s much bigger

Adriana I see Mars more as a stepping stone for our exploration of the rest of the solar system more than a permanent destination on the next door neighbour planet

Jim I think every body dreams about what’s beyond you can only hang in lower earth orbit at the international space station for so long before you say ok we are ready to go some where.

V/O 18 sec
Destination Mars is no longer a distant dream it’s the planet everyone - from space agencies, to astronauts to scientists- seem to agree is humanity’s next frontier ….it might be an average of 250 million kilometres away from Planet Earth but the Red Planet is the hot topic.

Jim Adams
in the days of Apollo in the 1960’s even then we were thinking about going to Mars but now more than ever the technology exists for us to be able to send humans to Mars and not just as a one time thing but as a permanent outpost that maybe some day could become a destination.

V/O 11 and a half sec
As NASA’s deputy chief technologist Jim Adam’s has been part of their solar exploration programmes since the 70’s and it’s the fourth planet from the sun that’s the crown jewel.

John: It must have been fascinating to have worked through the evolution in our understanding of Mars?
Jim: Absolutely in 1976 when we landed the Viking lander on the surface of Mars we dug down into the soil and where looking for signs of life even then we wanted to know the answer to one of the fundamental science questions Are we Alone..so we are looking for life and all we find are dty dusty iron laden rubble so we put it back down and decided Mars was probably not a place where we might find life beyond earth.

V/O 21 sec
And so NASA continued searching for signs of life in other planets in the solar system. It was over 20 years later, 2008, that the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter spotted water ice in the very region the Viking Lander had been…a small meteorite crater had exposed an area deeper below the surface.

John: Very small maybe the size of a cricket ball, but down inside the crater we could see a layer of white stuff we found it was water ice. The really interesting thing was if Viking had just dug 3 cms deeper we would have hit a layer of water ice on the surface of Mars it would have changed the whole history of exploration on Mars.
John: So 3 cm would have made it a very different mission
The missions we mounted into the solar systems would have been entirely focused on Mars instead of Mercury and Venus and all the others.

V/O 18 sec
It takes about 9 months to travel from Earth to Mars… and whilst gravity is not a problem being just under 40 % of ours…there are other factors that make Mars a hostile environment below freezing temperatures, extreme radiation, gale force winds and lack of oxygen.

John Is NASA still confident now that Mars is most likely to sustain life?
Jim: if you look at the features on Mars if you look at where the water is now and you look at the fact at one time had a coherent magnetic field then you can begin to understand how much earth like Mars must have been.

John: But when the time comes if we do discover that life existed on Mars …green man with antenna coming out of his head?
Jim: Its probably not aliens its probably microbes or algae we’ve detected methane gas that comes and goes volcanic or life decaying matter not cows on Mars…so methane might be coming from micrrobes that exist today so there might be life on Mars right now.

V/O 7 sec 05 23

In 2011 the Dutch NGO MARS 1 launched its plan to establish a permanent human settlement on Mars ….

BREAK SFX

V/O 13 and a half sec

in a matter of days they received 2 000 applicants from around the world all wanting a one way ticket to the Red Planet…A short list of 100 people were chosen three are form South Africa

V/O 9 sec
Adriana Marais, a 33 year old theoretical physicist, philosophy graduate and Head of Innovation at SAP Africa.

As a child I read a lot and always wished I was born in a different era, and I could be part of some revolution something like that. Now I realise the time is now and whether it would have been some early exploration mission or this one I would always be the kind of personality that would volunteer for it not as a sacrifice but as I said based on curiosity and the belief that I am up for the challenge.

V/O 6 and half sec
25 year old Divashen Govender a software engineer at Jumo World……….. astrophysics is his speciality.

Divashen:I’ve always wanted to go to Space its been a dream of mine and then this project came along with something that was beyond my ultimate goal.

V/O 5 and a half sec
23 year old Edwin Le Grange, a Control Room Operator for Macado Technologies

Edwin: It’s the biggest adventure….moon divers this has never been done before…everything we do has an opportunity to inspitre something bigger

LINK
The Mars mission requires a person with a certain type of personality someone who can tolerate isolation and boredom on the long journey to Mars and then kick into overdrive the minute they get there someone who is mentally resilient and who has excellent personal skills.

Divashen: You have to be adaptable and sensibility where you are not aggressively arrogant it’s a balance between having that leadership but knowing where your place is and how you fit in with the group.

John: The notion that being a one way trip?
Adriana: We are all survivors of one way trips the, I mean the Marais family my ancestors arrived in Saldhana Bay after stormy seas caused them to dock there this was 1688 …I’m a survivor of that one way trip and this is something that I’m proud of rather than thinking of it as some sort of sacrifice or tragedy these people came here to live and not to die and that is exactly what we plan to do on Mars.

Divashen: We know technology may advance to a point where a trip would come back but you have to have it in your mind that this is a one way trip and we are going with the intention of establishing a colony.

Edwin
John Why do you think they chose you?
Edwin: If I had to guess it’s the fact that I was working on game farms in isolation for so long and when you are 80 kms from the closest town you cant quickly drive in and buy a new screwdriver you have to innovate you have to think outside the box.
John You say you have come to terms with leaving your family behind but how comfortable are they with you going?
Edwin: Kept the one way part of the trip away from my grandmother she though I was coming back parts of the family have not come to terms with it they think I am crazy..

V/O 20 sec
Only 4 out of the 100 candidates will make it through the final selection process o be the first to settle on Mars…… the plan is that every two years new wannabee Martian’s would join the settlement. The date Mars 1 has for these first 4 Martians to leave earth has changed a lot, it’s now set at 2031.

John: And when you get there will Mars 1 have built at least a basic infrastructure?
Divashen: Supply missions and living modules will be sent ahead of time and then robots will unpack things when we think of robots we think of something small the size of a dog but hen you actually think of a rover well NASA’s rovers they are around that big .
John: Practicalities on living on Mars not being able to breathe having to get into a suit every time you go outside,
Adriana: Inside the settlement we will be able to walk around in regular clothes. Our time going outside will be limited by the fact that radiation on the surface of Mars is quiet extreme so having lived in Singapore and having heard how people live in Dubais I thin there are regions of earth where people don’t go outdoors much in certain weather conditions and this is how we will live in a more confined space but eventually the settlement will be expanded to the comparable size of a large underground mall, then further.

V/O 14 sec
NASA who have been in the game the longest, are way more cautious. They are not looking at a colony but rather astronauts spending 2 years at a time on Mars, doing research, a lot like the International Space Station.

John: NASA sees this as a 2 way trip?
Jim: Yes even in 1960’s we were looking for astronauts to go to the moon and we were having trouble closing the loop is what we call on the architecture that is to bring astronauts back there were some bold astronauts said volunteer 1 way not do that meet pres mandate send and return and that’s what we did.

V/O 12 and a half sec
But Elon Musk CEO of Spacex announced in June he wants the first manned mission to leave Earth in 2024 and his vision is a space colony a city on Mars.

Adrianna: SA Elon Musk has plans on a grander scale than most of us would possibly dream up as usual so he is planning to send 100 people at a time and possible in multiple launches of a 100 crew at a time.

LINK
SPACEX is currently developing technology that will allow humans to land on Mars in fact the company has already taken a giant leap in that direction thanks to its resupply mission to the INT SS its developed a rocket that can travel into space and then return to earth and land safely.

Jim: The whole idea of a reusable rocket has been elusive for a long time so when SPACEX announced they were going to fly their first stage back to landing zone it was inspiring. And the fact is they tried it first 2 times it didn’t work, their was a couple of explosions they kept on trying and now have it right.

Adriana; this will reduce launch costs by over 50% so imagine how many of us would have flown in an aeroplane if aeroplanes had kind of technologies were used once then re built from scratch

LINK
The successful Mars 1 candidates will undergo 10 years of training and no doubt that will involve how to become completely self sustaining including growing your own food and even making your own fuel.

Edwin: I’m one of the few exceptions in the group I’ve never studied I’ve only got matric behind my name even they have to go through the full 10 years.

Divashen: Then there’s the entire, social side of it , governance structures with 4 people does not make sense to have a governance structure but as the colony grows what’s going to happen then. I think it would be pretty cool if an entirely new way of thinking comes about where we look at science and use observation to shape our world.

John: Its interesting it might be a society that is driven and guided by knowledge as opposed to a sense of spirituality?
Divashen: Exactly, there may be a small spiritual element that keeps people going but effectively you are relying on your science and technology, if you are relying on something to survive that becomes your focus.

V/O 19 sec
In 1903 the Wright Brothers took their first flight 100 metres in a little wooden plane, less than 70 years later Man was standing on the moon if we can do that in 66 years how difficult is Mars, living in this period of accelerated development in science and technology

Jim: It’s not about the 1 person but the benefits of effort to get there and there will be benefits to society …problems on earth solved because of effort journey to Mars.

Now I realise the time is now and whether it would have been some early exploration mission or this one I would always be the kind of personality that would volunteer for it not as a sacrifice but as I said based on curiosity and the belief that I am up for the challenge. V/O 6 and half sec 25 year old Divashen Govender a software engineer at Jumo World……….. astrophysics is his speciality. Divashen:I’ve always wanted to go to Space its been a dream of mine and then this project came along with something that was beyond my ultimate goal. V/O 5 and a half sec 23 year old Edwin Le Grange, a Control Room Operator for Macado Technologies Edwin: It’s the biggest adventure….moon divers this has never been done before…everything we do has an opportunity to inspitre something bigger LINK The Mars mission requires a person with a certain type of personality someone who can tolerate isolation and boredom on the long journey to Mars and then kick into overdrive the minute they get there someone who is mentally resilient and who has excellent personal skills. Divashen: You have to be adaptable and sensibility where you are not aggressively arrogant it’s a balance between having that leadership but knowing where your place is and how you fit in with the group. John: The notion that being a one way trip? Adriana: We are all survivors of one way trips the, I mean the Marais family my ancestors arrived in Saldhana Bay after stormy seas caused them to dock there this was 1688 …I’m a survivor of that one way trip and this is something that I’m proud of rather than thinking of it as some sort of sacrifice or tragedy these people came here to live and not to die and that is exactly what we plan to do on Mars. Divashen: We know technology may advance to a point where a trip would come back but you have to have it in your mind that this is a one way trip and we are going with the intention of establishing a colony. Edwin John Why do you think they chose you? Edwin: If I had to guess it’s the fact that I was working on game farms in isolation for so long and when you are 80 kms from the closest town you cant quickly drive in and buy a new screwdriver you have to innovate you have to think outside the box. John You say you have come to terms with leaving your family behind but how comfortable are they with you going? Edwin: Kept the one way part of the trip away from my grandmother she though I was coming back parts of the family have not come to terms with it they think I am crazy.. V/O 20 sec Only 4 out of the 100 candidates will make it through the final selection process o be the first to settle on Mars…… the plan is that every two years new wannabee Martian’s would join the settlement. The date Mars 1 has for these first 4 Martians to leave earth has changed a lot, it’s now set at 2031. John: And when you get there will Mars 1 have built at least a basic infrastructure? Divashen: Supply missions and living modules will be sent ahead of time and then robots will unpack things when we think of robots we think of something small the size of a dog but hen you actually think of a rover well NASA’s rovers they are around that big . John: Practicalities on living on Mars not being able to breathe having to get into a suit every time you go outside, Adriana: Inside the settlement we will be able to walk around in regular clothes. Our time going outside will be limited by the fact that radiation on the surface of Mars is quiet extreme so having lived in Singapore and having heard how people live in Dubais I thin there are regions of earth where people don’t go outdoors much in certain weather conditions and this is how we will live in a more confined space but eventually the settlement will be expanded to the comparable size of a large underground mall, then further. V/O 14 sec NASA who have been in the game the longest, are way more cautious. They are not looking at a colony but rather astronauts spending 2 years at a time on Mars, doing research, a lot like the International Space Station. John: NASA sees this as a 2 way trip? Jim: Yes even in 1960’s we were looking for astronauts to go to the moon and we were having trouble closing the loop is what we call on the architecture that is to bring astronauts back there were some bold astronauts said volunteer 1 way not do that meet pres mandate send and return and that’s what we did. V/O 12 and a half sec But Elon Musk CEO of Spacex announced in June he wants the first manned mission to leave Earth in 2024 and his vision is a space colony a city on Mars. Adrianna: SA Elon Musk has plans on a grander scale than most of us would possibly dream up as usual so he is planning to send 100 people at a time and possible in multiple launches of a 100 crew at a time. LINK SPACEX is currently developing technology that will allow humans to land on Mars in fact the company has already taken a giant leap in that direction thanks to its resupply mission to the INT SS its developed a rocket that can travel into space and then return to earth and land safely. Jim: The whole idea of a reusable rocket has been elusive for a long time so when SPACEX announced they were going to fly their first stage back to landing zone it was inspiring. And the fact is they tried it first 2 times it didn’t work, their was a couple of explosions they kept on trying and now have it right. Adriana; this will reduce launch costs by over 50% so imagine how many of us would have flown in an aeroplane if aeroplanes had kind of technologies were used once then re built from scratch LINK The successful Mars 1 candidates will undergo 10 years of training and no doubt that will involve how to become completely self sustaining including growing your own food and even making your own fuel. Edwin: I’m one of the few exceptions in the group I’ve never studied I’ve only got matric behind my name even they have to go through the full 10 years. Divashen: Then there’s the entire, social side of it , governance structures with 4 people does not make sense to have a governance structure but as the colony grows what’s going to happen then. I think it would be pretty cool if an entirely new way of thinking comes about where we look at science and use observation to shape our world. John: Its interesting it might be a society that is driven and guided by knowledge as opposed to a sense of spirituality? Divashen: Exactly, there may be a small spiritual element that keeps people going but effectively you are relying on your science and technology, if you are relying on something to survive that becomes your focus. V/O 19 sec In 1903 the Wright Brothers took their first flight 100 metres in a little wooden plane, less than 70 years later Man was standing on the moon if we can do that in 66 years how difficult is Mars, living in this period of accelerated development in science and technology Jim: It’s not about the 1 person but the benefits of effort to get there and there will be benefits to society …problems on earth solved because of effort journey to Mars.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Have you got what it takes to get a one way ticket to Mars
metadata.Summary: Have you got what it takes to get a one way ticket to the Red planet Has science become a reality show? Five South Africans Divashen Govender, Kobus Vermeulen, Adriana Marais, Edwin le Grange and Alexandra Doyle have been shortlisted as part of a group of 100 participants from across the globe looking for a one-way ticket to Mars. In 2013, 2 000 people from across the globe initially applied to go to the red planet, a voyage scheduled to take place in 2018. Now the group has been fine-tuned to 100 There are 50 men and 50 women who successfully passed the second round. The candidates come from all around the world, namely 39 from the Americas, 31 from Europe, 16 from Asia, 7 from Africa, and 7 from Oceania. Is this crazy suicide mission or what or a bona fida science research project; a revival of the golden age of discovery where explorers left their homes to begin new civilisations ..the video used to inspire the 2000 people who initially signed is a mix between Survivors and The Hunger Games.
metadata.Further information: The objective of Dutch non-profit Mars One is simple: to establish a permanent human settlement on the red planet. They will begin training candidates for space travel up until its 2024 planned launch, when – if all goes well – teams of successful candidates from around the world will form part of the first human colony on Mars. And a lot of people don’t think this is an impossibility – life on Mars -like South African, Elon Musk, founder of space transport services company SpaceX, who has said recently that he was hopeful that humans could be taken to Mars in the next 10 to 12 years. “I think it’s certainly possible for that to occur. The thing that matters long term is to have a self-sustaining city on Mars to make life multiplanetary. That will define a fundamental bifurcation of the future of human civilisation. We’ll either be a multiplanet species and out there among the stars, or a single-planet species until some eventual extinction event, natural or man-made.” Candidate,Adriana Marais, a PhD student in quantum biology at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, “What the first colonisers will do on Mars is really the pinnacle of four billion years of evolution, I would volunteer to leave my life on Earth behind to see what’s out there. I’m prepared to sacrifice my personal joys, sorrows and day-to-day life for this idea, this adventure, this achievement that would not be mine but that of all humanity.” Candidate, Kobus Vermeulen, a 31-year-old from Pretoria has climbed Kili­man­jaro and skydived, said that Mars was the next big adventure. He has not romanticised the harsh realities of “yummy dehydrated army food” until the colony has established its food-growing mechanisms or that, if chosen, he would be leaving his old life behind. “In the end, you are exchanging all those things for new experiences on a new planet … you become part of humankind’s quest for long-term survival in what is, as it turns out, a very hostile universe.” Many of the South African candidates say that they would like to be buried on Mars, or to dedicate their bodies or organs to remaining crew members. But this may contaminate the planet and could also pose a problem to space science. With aid of visuals, artistic renditions of Mars, and real footage taken from the various missions we will explore how real this process will be and possible enlighten some of our candidates who despite ( apparently) rigorous research were not aware of the harshness of the Martian environment. Asked what they believed their days on Mars would involve, some said they would go for long walks to explore the planet, ­others that they would be growing food in Mars’s mineral-rich soil. Science and what has been discovered about Mars will be tested against some of the perceptions put out by Mars One. Out of the 100 chosen it will be 24 who eventually join the first settlement team, the ultimate Big Brother Challenge
